cases.situation: Leo has no safety-net record at all, so the default applies: protection on, the starter size, nothing saved. He has $800 spare this month and is looking at a $500 purchase. It is bought on 15 November 2026 (today), paid in one go. A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,400 and everyday spending $800 ($500 of it on essentials).
cases.why: No record means the default: protection on, a starter size of one month of essential costs ($1,400 bills + $500 essential everyday spending = $1,900), and $0 saved. Only money already in the net is protected, so nothing is held back (D-35): $800 spare - $500 = $300 left. $300 is not under the tight floor of $220 (a tenth of $1,400 bills + $800 everyday spending), so the answer is the amber "Fits, but no safety net", with "Nothing is saved for emergencies yet. One month of essential costs is about $1,900. 1 month is a start; 3 to 6 months is common." It never says a safety net is "untouched" (D-25).

She is looking at a $600 purchase. It is bought on 15 November 2026 (today), paid in one go. A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,200 and everyday spending $800 ($500 of it on essentials).

At $300 spare a month it is refilled in about 1 month (200 / 300, rounded up): "Dips into your safety net", with the month figure shown as -$200, not $0.

cases.why: Spare money says yes ($800 - $700 = $100), but the day-by-day path does not. The $400 of everyday spending still to come is spread evenly, $25 a day over the 16 days from 15 to 30 November. After rent on the 20th the account goes below $0, reaching $1,400 - $600 rent - $300 everyday spending (15 to 26 November) - $700 = -$200 on 26 November. So the answer says it "needs $200 from your safety net until 27 Nov", the next payday. The path must stay above the net (FIN-02), so this is "Dips into your safety net", not a plain "Fits". cases.persona: Maya, freelancer, no pay series (invented, D-52)
cases.situation: Maya is a freelancer with no scheduled pay. Over the last six months (April to September) she was paid $3,100, $2,900, $3,000, $3,200, $2,800 and $3,000, always on the 5th; her lowest month was $2,800. $3,000 came in on 1 October. By 3 October she has paid rent $1,000 and phone $200 (bills $1,200 in all) and spent $50; her $200 monthly transfer to savings goes out on the 6th and has not gone yet. $2,250 is in her everyday account and $3,000 sits in her savings account marked as her safety net (locked, the default). She is looking at a $60 purchase. It is bought on 3 October 2026 (today), paid in one go. A usual month: pay $3,000 (her own steady figure), bills $1,200, a $200 transfer to savings on the 6th and everyday spending $800 (all of it on essentials).
cases.why: D-52: with no pay series but six full months of history, pay is expected on her usual payday (the 5th) at her lowest month ($2,800), so November and December each bring $2,800 on the 5th. October: $3,000 in - $1,200 bills - $200 to savings - $50 spent - $750 everyday still to come = $800 left; $800 - $60 = $740, a plain "Fits" from this month's money. $740 is over the tight floor of $200 (a tenth of $1,200 bills + $800 everyday spending). The safety net's starter size is $2,000 ($1,200 bills + $800 essential spending), so $1,000 of her $3,000 is extra savings. D-67: the $200 saving leaves her everyday account on the 6th of each month, on every path. Her everyday account alone: $2,250 - $60 - $200 on 6 October - $750 everyday in October = $1,240 on 31 October; $1,200 of bills on 1 November and about $26.67 a day of everyday spending take it to about $13.33 on 1 November and about $13.33 below $0 on 2 November, lowest about $66.67 below $0 on 4 November before her pay on the 5th. With the $1,000 of extra savings the path stays well above $0, so the net is not needed and the answer adds, as a timing fact (D-58), "Move $66.67 from your savings to your everyday account by 2 November."
cases.plannerNote: From the plan-18 audit (Maya $60). Restated in 05.4-51 with the D-58 saving field: the $200 saving on the 6th (not moved yet) replaces the earlier workaround of a $200 bill already paid (bills $1,400 -> $1,200, everyday account $2,050 -> $2,250), so the usual month and October's $740 are unchanged. Hand move-by (D-58, D-67): $66.67 by 2 November; with no saving the account alone stays about $133.33 above $0 and there is no move-by line, and at $500 the move-by is $506.67 with the saving against $306.67 without (20,000 more, the persona Maya's audit figure). Engine (05.4-51 rules): fits_month, null, month 74000, move_money_by {6667, 2026-11-02}, cash ok with its low point 93,333 on 2026-11-04. Hand, plain calculator and engine agree.

Your usual month is $300 short." How long your money lasts = spare money + extra savings, never the locked safety net, divided by the usual shortfall. $4,350 / $300 = 14 months; $60 does not take a whole month off. The depletion lines show (D-54): the usual month is $300 short and $300 a month in lower costs or higher income balances it. The net is locked (D-61), so no line says how long it would last (D-66).
